name: Gray Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Breeds western north america; winters to southern mexico
description: Drab, pale-gray flycatcher with little plumage contrast; very similar to other flycatchers, especially Dusky and Hammond's. Often best identified by unique habit of wagging tail downward.

name: Two-barred Warbler
rangeDescription: Southern siberia to mongolia and manchuria; winters to southeastern asia
description: A small songbird, greenish above, white below, with black-bordered white supercilium and thin white wingbars. Larger and more contrastingly marked than Yellow-browed Warbler, which has weaker wingbars and a generally stouter appearance.

name: Pied Oystercatcher
rangeDescription: Coastal australia including tasmania, and southern new guinea, aru, and kai islands
description: Heavy-set shorebird with long, thick reddish bill, black and white plumage, and thick pale-pink feet and legs. Usually coastal, but sometimes found on wetter pastures close to the coast.

name: Northern Red-billed Hornbill
rangeDescription: Sierra leone to somalia and southward to tanzania
description: A fairly small, slim, long-tailed hornbill. Note the red bill, the pink or red bare facial skin, and the heavily spotted back.

name: Pale-rumped Swift
rangeDescription: Eastern ecuador to eastern peru, northern bolivia, and western amazonian brazil
description: Medium-sized swift with a strongly contrasting rump patch. Dark slaty gray, with a lighter gray throat and a large white rump patch.

name: Henderson Island Reed Warbler
rangeDescription: Henderson island (pitcairn archipelago)
description: A large warbler with a variably white head and body. Crown and uppersides often mottled olive-brown and white, underside often tinted yellow.

name: Thick-billed Lark
rangeDescription: Stony desert of northwestern africa to jordan and northwestern arabia
description: Unmistakable large lark with a huge pale bill, dark-speckled cheek and breast, round cheek spot, and prominent white areas on the wing in flight. Males have more contrasting plumage than females.

name: Sulu Pygmy Woodpecker
rangeDescription: Sulu archipelago (bongao, jolo, tawitawi, sanga sanga, and sibutu)
description: A small woodpecker of lowland wooded areas on the Sulu Islands. Dark brown above with some white spots on the back, a white rump, throat, and underparts with faint streaking, and buffy sides of the chest.

name: Usambara Thrush
rangeDescription: Mountains of northeastern tanzania (pare and usambara mountains)
description: A typical thrush with brownish upperparts and paler rufous-and-gray underparts. Also note the darker face, yellow bill, and striped throat.

name: Wattled Guan
rangeDescription: Montane forest of western venezuela to northern peru
description: Distinctive guan: all black with cerulean bill, yellowish-orange legs, and thin yellow dewlap. Could be confused with Sickle-winged Guan, which is smaller and has warm brown underparts.

name: Pygmy Antwren
rangeDescription: Eastern colombia to the guianas, amazonian brazil, and northern bolivia
description: Tiny, very short-tailed antwren of rainforest midstory and lower canopy. Males are yellow with white head and wing bars, and extensive black streaking on the head and back; females are similar to males, but have a red-orange wash on the head and more extensive streaking in the breast.

name: Brown-chested Jungle Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Breeds southeastern china; winters in southwestern thailand and the thai-malay peninsula
description: Drab and lethargic flycatcher of extensively forested regions; most common in hills and mountain valleys but also ranges into lowlands. Sexes are similar: brown above and white below with tan suffusions on the flanks and neck.

name: Yemen Warbler
rangeDescription: Acacia scrub of southern yemen and southwestern saudi arabia
description: Unusual and distinctive warbler of the southwest Arabian highlands. Gray-brown, with a darker cap, paler throat, and pale eye.

name: Red-eyed Puffback
rangeDescription: Lowlands of senegambia to southeastern democratic republic of the congo, northern angola, and uganda
description: A shrike-like bird of thickets in secondary forest and forest edge, often seen high above the ground. Has a bicolored appearance, being wholly white below and almost entirely iridescent black above except for a white rump, a red eye, and the female’s white lores.

name: Purple-crowned Lorikeet
rangeDescription: Semiarid lowlands of southwestern and southeastern australia, including kangaroo island
description: Small green lorikeet with pale blue underparts. Note orange and yellow check patch, purple crown, yellow above the bill, and red patches in front of the eyes.

name: Ivory-backed Woodswallow
rangeDescription: Sulawesi region, including lembeh (off northeast), and banggai and sula islands (off eastern sulawesi)
description: A chunky slate-gray and white bird with a heavy, pale blue bill. A gregarious bird of forest and forest edge in the lowlands and mountains.

name: Mountain Avocetbill
rangeDescription: Central andes of colombia to northern peru (amazonas to la libertad)
description: Scarce Andean hummingbird with a short, awl-like bill that is upturned at the tip. Mostly green, and streaked with white on the underparts; also note the buff tinge to belly and white spot behind the eye.

name: Rio de Janeiro Antbird
rangeDescription: Southeastern brazil (southern bahia and eastern minas gerais to rio de janeiro)
description: Medium-sized gray antbird with a long tail. An inhabitant of the understory of dense humid forest.

name: Abyssinian Longclaw
rangeDescription: High grassland of ethiopia
description: A large and relatively colorful member of the pipit family. Note the black necklace, orange throat, and partially yellow eye-stripe.

name: Moluccan Owlet-nightjar
rangeDescription: Northern moluccas (halmahera, kasiruta, and bacan)
description: A large owlet-nightjar of lowland and foothill forests. Rufous or dark brown morphs present and also intergrades.
